text:
sam: FYI customer reported sustained 5xx/timeouts on hosted inference around 11:05 UTC. They see P95/P99 spikes and a bunch of request queue timeouts. attaching quick notes.

anita: Customer: 'Paylance' — says >~2% of requests are 504s, errors are timeouts from our gateway. They sent a sample trace.

sam: repro from trace: requests pile up in continuous-batcher backlog, queue_depth reported ~7800/8192, dequeue latency climbing.

jordan: @oncall-sre can you check batcher pool and kv-cache metrics? Might be kv thrash during longseqs causing slow dequeues.

oncall-sre: running quick checks now. `curl -sS http://ops-metrics.local/metrics | grep continuous_batch` -> returned current_queue_depth=7789, avg_dequeue_ms=1430, p99_dequeue_ms=3210

ops-bot: ALERT: hosted-gateway.queue_depth >= 75% (7789/8192) for tenant=paylance for 6m. Incident created: INC-1747774321.

karim: That queue_depth is effectively saturating the batchers. When queue hits high watermark we see timeouts at gateway due to request deadline. Two quick mitigations: 1) enable temporary passive-shed to drop very large seq requests, 2) increase continuous-batcher.queue_limit to 12k for affected hostpool.

anita: Customer is on hosted standard plan; prefer no dropped requests if possible. Can we scale up batcher workers or shift traffic to a larger hostpool?

jordan: Scaling path: increase pool size by +2 workers and rotate traffic. I can trigger scale, but need approval for capacity burn. Expected time to warm: ~45s to be ready.

sam: go ahead with scale +2. also try to reduce kv-cache eviction churn. karim, any quick param to tune cache?

karim: yes — reduce kv_cache.max_entries from 500k -> 300k and bump kv_cache.eviction_threshold to 0.8 so it evicts less frequently. Also enable prefix-kv sticky caching for common routes. I'll push a safe rollout.

oncall-sre: scale command run: `infractl pool scale --pool hosted-batcher-usw2-3 --add 2 --reason "Paylance queue surge"` -> API accepted, workers provisioning.

ops-bot: DEPLOYMENT: hosted-batcher-usw2-3 +2 workers requested by jordan. status: provisioning.

oncall-sre: after +2 workers came up (approx 60s), queue dropped to 4100, avg_dequeue_ms -> 540ms, p99_dequeue_ms -> 980ms. Gateway 504s reduced to ~0.3%.

anita: Customer confirmed partial recovery; still seeing occasional tail timeouts at high seq lengths. They provided payload examples (long context ~20k tokens).

karim: longseqs are the tail contributor. We should add longseq handling: route >8k tokens to a dedicated longseq slot or throttle client with guidance. For immediate relief, enable per-tenant max_seq_length=8192 and respond with 413 + hint when exceeded.

sam: for hosted customers we need smoother UX than errors. Suggested interim: router fallback to a lower-plex model variant that handles longseqs at lower throughput but avoids queue clog. Could we configure an automatic variant fallback?

jordan: we have a compatible variant (llama-longseq-16k-quant) that has lower throughput but higher mem. I can add a policy to route tenant=paylance to that variant for requests >8k tokens. Will take ~2m to update routing rules and warm caches.

ops-bot: ROUTE-UPDATE job started by jordan.

oncall-sre: route update applied. Observed KV cache warm-up; within 3m queue depth steady ~1500 and p99_dequeue_ms ~450ms. No 504s in last 5m.

anita: passing customer the mitigation steps and timeline. asked for postmortem and permanent fix.

sam: TL;DR actions: 1) scaled pool +2 transiently, 2) adjusted kv_cache eviction params, 3) enabled variant fallback for longseqs, 4) incident INC-1747774321 opened.

karim: follow-ups: add longseq routing policy to docs, add auto-scale policy for hosted-batcher when queue_depth >70% for >2m, and add tenant quota guidance for token limits in onboarding.

anita: I'll own the customer comms and the postmortem. Assigning follow-ups in tracker. Thanks team :thumbsup:

sam: marking incident stable. will close after postmortem.
